output.summary: New-operator and bar explanations are not supported by the record. New operators run no worse than experienced staff (E14). The hour-of-shift pattern comes from batch tag-writing, not machining time (E3), so fatigue cannot yet be tested. Measurement is stable and customer rejects rise (E4, E5), so the out-of-tolerance increase is real. Spindle deterioration is documented (E9, E10) and fits the size and chatter mix (E12), but it is confounded with the bar change. Returning to 8-hour shifts, reporting a root cause to Halvard, cutting CMM sampling, and sanctioning new operators are not justified. The preferred step is the staged spindle service with a Tamsworth/Corvane comparison, which discriminates between the live hypotheses. Evidence is insufficient to commit to a substantive intervention.
